Mathematical consequence: let r be the positive’s rank among all eligible catalog items. Select the evaluated model’s exact top-K alternatives, excluding the positive, using the same scores, filtering and deterministic tie-breaking. Its rank within that panel plus the positive is min(r, K+1): exact through K, then right-censored as “rank ≥ K+1.” Thus panel HR@h equals full-catalog HR@h for h≤K. Beyond K, ranks become indistinguishable; reciprocal rank and positive-versus-alternative win rate acquire artificial floors. This identity requires exact retrieval over the same eligible catalog; approximate retrieval or a restricted pool breaks it.

Hardness is guaranteed by selection: these are the model’s highest-scoring competitors. Low win rates or negative score margins therefore do not independently diagnose poor discrimination, preference mismatch or miscalibration. Different models select different panels, although the rank identity still permits comparison of their full-catalog top-K success. Unobserved alternatives also need not be genuinely irrelevant; research documents false negatives among highly ranked candidates ([Cai et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.05072)). With score ties, strict-greater counting, pessimistic ranking and deterministic tie-breaking yield different results; an all-tied model can appear perfect under strict-greater counting. Report ties and use one consistent ordering throughout.

Uniform negatives answer a different question. For N eligible alternatives and m sampled uniformly without replacement, the number outranking the positive is hypergeometric, with expectation m(r−1)/N under a fixed total ordering. Uniform panels can therefore retain information about deeper ranks while producing optimistic top-cutoff results; self-selected top-K panels saturate once r>K. Neither panel’s aggregate metrics are interchangeable: sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation ([Krichene and Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).
